summary: Your people's votes, for a price: {party official} wants the people who follow your lead to vote and work for {the slate}, and asks what you want for them.
realLife: One life: The Tammany leader said in 1905 that he started with one follower, a cousin, added two friends next door, and worked down the block until the district leaders came courting. Another: He grew up in Chicago's Bridgeport and became president of the Hamburg Athletic Club, which local Democrats helped fund, then rose from precinct captain to the state House in 1936.
gates: A recorded following: a club you lead or a street that follows you.
A contested primary or a race the party needs is coming.
choices: ask the rival faction what it offers
keep your people uncommitted and say so
put it to your people to vote on

branches.when: you ask for a public job in return
branches.then: Where the place has a civil service law on record, {party official} cannot simply deliver, and says so, or offers to help with the test.

branches.when: your first follower asks what he gets
branches.then: A cousin or friend who followed you first wants his share, and his tie depends on the answer.
The rival faction offers more. Taking it makes an enemy of {party official}.
Half work the polls and half quit, and the ones who quit blame you.
